note: GTF3C3 deficiency literature documents cerebellar atrophy, frontal lobe hypoplasia, and corpus callosum abnormalities, making this neuroimaging comparison plausible.

evidence.text: Brain MRI of patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants demonstrated brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, hypoplasia of the frontal lobes, and simplified gyral pattern.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern.

evidence.text: Affected individuals with recessive GTF3C3 variants presented with cerebellar and corpus callosum malformations, including progressive cerebral and marked cerebellar atrophy and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: The cohort presented with intellectual disability, variable nonfamilial facial features, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations.
